sections.content:
You know *acostumbrarse a* from B1 Unit 29 and *confiar en* from B1 Unit 40: many verbs go with a fixed preposition, and it often differs from English. *Consistir en* and *tratar* have also appeared in B1 word lists. Here are four verbs, each with its own preposition:

• *consistir en*: "to consist of". English says *of*, Spanish says *en*: *El trabajo consiste en contestar llamadas.*
• *derivar en*: "to lead to", "to end in". The result follows: *La discusión derivó en una pelea.*
• *tratarse de*: "to be about", "to be a matter of". It is always *se trata de*, third person singular, with no subject: *Se trata de un problema serio.*
• *abogar por*: "to speak in favour of", "to campaign for": *Los vecinos abogan por una calle sin carros.*

items.spanish: La propuesta deriva de un estudio.
items.english: The proposal comes from a study.

items.spanish: El estudio derivó en una propuesta.
items.english: The study led to a proposal.

items.spanish: El libro trata de dos hermanos.
items.english: The book is about two brothers.

sections.content: Watch the direction of *derivar*: *derivar de* looks back to the origin, *derivar en* looks forward to the result. Also, *tratar de* + infinitive means "to try to", while *se trata de* + noun says what something is about. Never say *consiste de*.
